clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms: the order says 'I do hereby exempt Adrian J. Pieters from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until December 1, 1937'. Recorded as 1937-12-01, inclusive (runs through the end of that day) under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling; the exclusive alternative ends the exemption when that day began. Actor: EO 7478 itself. Later events: EO 7750 of November 23, 1937, a separate further exemption of the same employee until December 1, 1938.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl (a common-crawl capture, so the page can be re-fetched from the recorded WARC location) has the heading 'Executive Order 7478—Exemption of Adrian J. Pieters From Compulsory Retirement for Age', the date 1936-10-24, which agrees with the date line of the held text, and a text_sha256 equal to the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. EO 7478 (October 24, 1936, Franklin D. Roosevelt) exempts Adrian J. Pieters, principal agronomist, Bureau of Plant Industry, Department of Agriculture, who reaches retirement age in November 1936, from section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 and continues the employee in the service until December 1, 1937. Identity: number, date, person and title agree across the APP page record, the held text's date line and the census register. Legal reading: a single time-limited grant that ends by its own terms on 1937-12-01, inclusive. Later orders naming the same employee are held and added to this packet as source-supplement excerpts: EO 7750 (November 23, 1937) recites Pieters as 'exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of one year by Executive Order No. 7478 of October 24, 1936' and further exempts the employee until December 1, 1938. Each is recorded as a later event on the clause (clauses.csv). Extension reading, decided on the texts: each later order is a new exercise of the section 204 proviso with its own period. None says that the earlier order 'is amended' or alters its date; each recites the earlier exemption as a past grant ('who was exempted ... by Executive Order No. ...') and grants a further exemption for a new period. The strike-and-insert ruling does not apply because nothing is struck or inserted. So this order's own command ended on its own stated date, inclusive (exclusive alternative: ended when that day began), and each later order is recorded as a later event naming the same employee; the employee's exempt status continued without a gap under the later orders. The alternative reading, that the later orders prolonged this order's command, would put its first end at the last later order's stated end (1938-12-01, inclusive); the texts do not support it, because no later order operates on this order's text. The searches below found no further order naming this person after EO 7750. Searches made on 2026-10-28: (1) every census-register title (jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv) containing 'retire' or 'exempt', for the person's surname and full name; (2) a full-text search of every held order text under jobs/*/output/texts (clause-drafts copies excluded) for the person's name; (3) a citation search of the same texts for this order's number in the forms 'No. N', 'Order N' and 'Orders N'. The machine USC and eCFR citation searches (complete, 0 hits) exclude a current-law reference; the OFR catalog search starts in 1937 and is not relied on alone. Authority: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), whose proviso lets the President exempt a person from automatic separation at retirement age. No held source shows section 204 repealed or amended before this order's stated end. The held texts of EO 7945 (August 4, 1938) and EO 8231 (August 31, 1939) grant further exemptions under section 204 (cited there as 5 U.S.C. 715a), which corroborates that the statutory scheme was still in force through the stated end of every exemption submitted in this batch (the latest is January 1, 1938).

Any annuity or retirement-credit consequence flows from the retirement statutes, not from the order, and does not keep the order operative: the order commands nothing after its stated date. The later orders (EO 7750) recite it as a past grant and grant new exemptions; they do not keep this order operative.
